title: Chapter 7 — Ivie's Fees
description: The school wants ₦120,000 and a letter stating "the parent's source of income". And another mother at the PTA meeting has seen you before.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A letter from Ivie's school, Bright Future College, Ikorodu: "Second term fees: ₦120,000. Parents are also required to submit a statement of their source of income, as part of our new values policy."

beats.speaker: ivie
beats.text: (on the phone) Mummy, they're making everybody do it. Tobi's dad wrote "oil and gas". Chiamaka's mum wrote "importation". What will you write?

variants.text: (on the phone, very carefully) Mummy. The form. Whatever you write... just write something they will accept. Please.

options.text: "Hospitality and catering." It's not a lie.
Go to the school and tell the proprietress in person.
Pay a man at Ojota to make a letter from "Sugar Holdings Ltd".

beats.objective: Take the danfo to Ikorodu. Bright Future College.

beats.speaker: proprietress
beats.text: (Mrs. Adéwálé, in her office, after you finish) Madam. (She takes off her glasses.) I have one parent who sells "importation" that I know is Indian hemp, and another whose "oil and gas" is a filling station he stole from his brother. (She signs the form herself.) Your daughter is top of her class. That is the only income I care about.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The PTA meeting. You wear your church clothes. Halfway through the bursar's speech, a woman across the hall stares at you. You know her. Her husband comes to Sugar Palace every second Thursday.

beats.speaker: player
beats.text: She is crossing the hall towards you.

options.text: Smile. "Madam. How is Oga? Tell him the pepper soup misses him."
"I think you are mistaking me." Hold her eyes.

beats.objective: Raise ₦120,000 for Ivie's fees. Sell drinks at the bar, take door duty, anything honest.

beats.speaker: ivie
beats.text: (a voice note) Mummy, the bursar said "paid in full". In front of everybody. (A pause.) I know how hard it is. I'm not stupid. Thank you.

beats.title: Ivie's Fees
beats.summary: One hundred and twenty thousand naira and a form asking where it came from. You answered, one way or another.
